# README and three blog posts link maintainers' freed GitHub logins

## Context

Three maintainer accounts were renamed: `neo-gpt` → `neo-gpt-euclid` (Euclid), `neo-gemini-pro` → `neo-gemini-julia` (Julia), `neo-fable` → `neo-fable-mnemosyne` (Mnemosyne). GitHub does not redirect a renamed user's profile, so links to the old logins return 404, and anyone can register those logins.

Observed 2026-10-20 ~10:15Z on `origin/dev` 4844087a77:

- `gh api users/neo-gpt`, `users/neo-gemini-pro` and `users/neo-fable` return 404. `neo-gpt-euclid`, `neo-gemini-julia` and `neo-fable-mnemosyne` resolve.
- They are the same accounts: `gh pr view` reports #19688's author as `neo-gpt-euclid`, #19740's as `neo-gemini-julia` and #19809's as `neo-fable-mnemosyne`.

neomjs.com builds from the published npm package, so whatever these files hold at the 13.3.0 cut is what the site serves until 13.4.

## The Problem

Today these are dead links. If someone registers one of the freed logins, the README's maintainer table vouches for that stranger as a Neo maintainer.

## The Architectural Reality

A whole-tree `git grep` for the link targets `github.com/(neo-gpt|neo-gemini-pro|neo-fable)` on `origin/dev` 4844087a77 finds:

| File | What links or names a freed login |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | three rows of *The Maintainer Team* (Mnemosyne, Julia, Euclid). The roster sentence under it also names `@neo-fable`, `@neo-gemini-pro` and `@neo-gpt` as text. |
| `learn/blog/cross-family-verification.md` | Euclid's link |
| `learn/blog/the-organism-already-existed.md` | Mnemosyne's preface link and handle, plus the closing byline's handle |
| `learn/blog/where-an-agent-institution-sits.md` | Mnemosyne's byline link |
| `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v13.3.0.md` | "Who builds it" and the changelog. Cut-prep PR #19784 (head 5a4a62da87) already rewrites both. |

Design authority: README's *The Maintainer Team* says "We are a team of named maintainers working across the `neomjs` repositories". Each row's Maintainer column links that maintainer's account, so a 404 link contradicts its own row.

## The Fix

In `README.md` (the three table rows' link text and URL, and the roster sentence) and the three blog posts (link URLs and byline handle text), replace each old login with its current one. Nothing else changes. #19784 changes README.md's line 150; these hunks sit at lines 133–137 and 239, so the two PRs do not conflict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: on the PR head, `git grep -nE 'github\.com/(neo-gpt|neo-gemini-pro|neo-fable)([)"/#?]|$)'` matches only `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v13.3.0.md`, whose rewrite #19784 owns.
- [ ] AC-2: every `github.com/<login>` link in README.md's maintainer table resolves (`gh api users/<login>`).
- [ ] AC-3: README.md's roster sentence and the three blog posts name the current logins, and the diff changes no other line.

## Out of Scope

- `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v13.3.0.md`, owned by #19784.
- Unlinked historical prose that records the login of its time, such as signatures like "I am Euclid, `@neo-gpt`" in `learn/agentos/**` and ADR quotes.
- The generated `AGENTS.md` roster and the skills that name the old logins. Their source is `neo-agent-skills`, so they are captured as a defect-note, not edited here.
- Registering the freed logins so nobody else can take them. That is account creation, which is the operator's call.

## Related

- #19784 (the release notes' logins), #19740 and #19845 (roster rows), neomjs/pages#45 (the issues showcase's renamed authors).
